$comment: Phase-2 wave-1 OpenConnector ingestion config for TenderNed (NL national procurement platform). Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_tenderned.py's endpoint, field semantics and pagination shape, but ingests the full chronological /publicaties feed instead of looping over Specter's ~30 relevance-scoring search terms: that keyword harvesting was Specter's own DB-side classification layer, not a constraint of the TenderNed API itself. Confirmed live 2026-07-05: GET /publicaties with no `searchTerm` returns the full feed (144,345 elements at time of writing), sorted by publicatieDatum desc, 0-indexed Spring-style pagination. Public, unauthenticated API - no secrets required. `categorySlug`/`relevance` classification is intentionally left unmapped (out of scope for this native ingestion connector; a downstream classification step is a W2 concern). `cpvCodes` maps to a literal empty array because the /publicaties list endpoint does not expose CPV codes at all (confirmed live) - TED is the wave-1 source that actually populates that field. KNOWN LIMITATION: OpenConnector's pagination counter (`currentPage`, 1-based) does not line up with TenderNed's own 0-based `page` param beyond the first page - the engine's first HTTP call never sends a `page` param at all (so it correctly lands on TenderNed's true page 0), but its second call sends `page=2`, which is TenderNed's *third* page (0-indexed page 2), silently skipping TenderNed's second page. Harmless for the wave-1 single-page proof (maxPages temporarily set to 1 for the live spike test) but must be fixed - e.g. a `sourceConfig.pageOffset` knob - before this ships a genuine multi-page crawl in W2. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-05 end-to-end on the isolated spectr-spike instance (NC 34, OR 0.2.17-unstable.7, spectr register id=8): imported via POST /apps/openregister/api/configurations/import, maxPages temporarily patched to 1 on the live copy, run via POST /apps/openconnector/api/synchronizations/tenderned-to-spectr-tender/run - 50/50 tenders created correctly on the first pass, re-run reused the same 50 target objects (0 duplicates; register count unchanged at 82,000 active tender objects) confirming the synchronization-contract-keyed upsert prevents duplication on re-run, though the hash-based skip-vs-update optimisation did not trigger on that re-run for a reason not conclusively isolated (originHash was confirmed byte-identical before and after, so it isn't a hash-instability problem - plausibly the routine currentPage-reset write inside getAllObjectsFromApi() touching synchronization state on every call; worth a follow-up before relying on the skip path for cost/traffic savings in W2). One field-mapping defect was found and fixed by this live test: notice 431881 (a 'Vooraankondiging'/market-consultation type) has `procedure: {"code": "NA"}` with no `omschrijving` key at all - the bare dot-path mapping silently wrote the literal string 'procedure.omschrijving' into the target object's `procedure` field instead of leaving it empty (see IMPORT.md's mapping-engine gotcha). Fixed here by wrapping `procedure`/`typeOpdracht`/the hash mapping's `publicatiestatus` in explicit `{{ x|default('') }}` Twig expressions; 1/50 sampled notices hit this on the live run, so it is a real, not theoretical, edge case for this source. Also note: the openconnector build actually installed in the shared `nextcloud` container's custom_apps at test time was stale (v0.2.15, NC max-version capped at 32, and missing a `processRules()` int-cast fix present in the apps-extra git working tree as of commit 070eed6e) - the live verification used the git working tree's build (v0.2.16) instead, trimmed the same way (vendor/js/lib/appinfo/css/img/l10n/templates, no tests/openspec/dev-tooling/sourcemaps). The shared container's copy needs redeploying from a current build before this can be repeated against it directly.

objects.name: TenderNed
objects.description: Dutch national procurement platform (TenderNed) publications API v2. Public, unauthenticated, no documented rate-limit header contract. Feeds the spectr `tender` register/schema via the tenderned-to-spectr-tender synchronization.

objects.name: TenderNed Hash Mapping
objects.description: Narrows a raw TenderNed publication down to the fields that represent real content before hashing, for sourceHash change-detection (SynchronizationService::mapHashObject). Deliberately drops `aantalDagenTotSluitingsDatum` (a days-until-deadline counter that recomputes to a different value every day even when nothing about the tender itself changed) and `score`/`kenmerk` (per-search/internal fields irrelevant to a full-feed sync). Without this mapping every tender would look 'changed' on every run and dedup would never skip anything.

objects.name: TenderNed to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Maps a raw TenderNed /publicaties list item onto the spectr `tender` schema. Mirrors the field selection of concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_tenderned.py's upsert_tender(). All source field paths (publicatieId, aanbestedingNaam, opdrachtgeverNaam, opdrachtBeschrijving, publicatieDatum, sluitingsDatum, procedure.omschrijving, typeOpdracht.omschrijving, europees, link.href) confirmed live against a real /publicaties response on 2026-07-05.

objects.name: TenderNed to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Wave-1 ingestion sync: TenderNed /publicaties (full chronological feed, no searchTerm) -> spectr register, tender schema. `maxPages` ships at a conservative 10 (~500 notices/run) for the weekly job cadence below. For the live spike verification this was temporarily patched to 1 (single page, ~50 notices) directly on the isolated spectr-spike instance - see IMPORT.md and the spectr-spike live-test transcript; the git-committed default here stays at 10.

objects.name: TenderNed Weekly Sync
objects.description: Runs the tenderned-to-spectr-tender synchronization weekly, matching Specter's own tendril cadence (concurrentie-analyse weekly GitHub Actions sync, Sunday 02:00 UTC).
